findings.problem: The item says that 'the certified prescriber, not the pharmacy,' handles the Patient Agreement Form and ensures the patient receives a copy of it and of the Medication Guide. Nothing limits it to the REMS. Read alone, as a quick-review line is meant to be read, it tells a candidate that a pharmacy dispensing mifepristone has no part in getting the Medication Guide to the patient.
findings.rationale: The REMS does put the Patient Agreement Form, and ensuring the patient gets a copy of it and of the Medication Guide, on the certified prescriber (II.A.1.b.iii). The pharmacy requirements in II.A.2 do not mention the Guide. But the REMS does not displace 21 CFR 208.24(e): each authorized dispenser of a product for which a Medication Guide is required must provide it directly to the patient or the patient's agent when the product is dispensed. The Mifeprex carton carries the 208.24(d) instruction 'Dispense the accompanying Medication Guide to each patient'. The section teaches this correctly in orientation[8] ('Nothing in the REMS document displaces 21 CFR 208.24(e)') and in worked_examples[3].steps[4], so quick_review[13] contradicts the section's own point about who hands over the Guide at a certified Massachusetts pharmacy. Suggested repair: keep the 'not the pharmacy' contrast only for the REMS allocation. For example: 'Under the REMS the certified prescriber, not the pharmacy, handles the Patient Agreement Form and ensures the patient receives a copy of it and of the Medication Guide; the pharmacist who dispenses still provides the Guide under 21 CFR 208.24(e).' Severity is Low because the correct rule is stated in three other places in the section. The defect is recorded under actor_and_scope only, to avoid counting it twice.

results.summary: MINOR_EDIT, Low. I read the whole section: all 11 orientation paragraphs, every table cell, all 5 worked examples, all 21 retrieval prompts and answers, and every list field. I checked it against current official text: 21 CFR 208.1, 208.3, 208.20(a), 208.24 and 208.26 on eCFR (Part 208 unchanged since 2016); 21 U.S.C. 355-1 as in effect on 2026-09-15; FDA's November 2011 Medication Guide distribution guidance (still listed as final), including III.A.2 and Table 1; REMS@FDA and the 09/2025 Mifepristone REMS Document, read in full; FDA's mifepristone Q&A and information pages; FDA's clozapine REMS-removal Drug Safety Communication; and the DailyMed labeling for Mifeprex and Clozaril. Everything is accurate except one item. The 208.3 definitions, the 208.24(e) agent delivery, the 208.26(b) patient-request override and the limits on FDA's 208.26(a) power all match the text. The guidance is presented as nonbinding enforcement discretion, and Table 1 is transcribed correctly (inpatient; outpatient administration including the ED and outpatient surgery; direct to patient). The 355-1(e) and (f) elements, and their addressees, match the statute. The section never states a pharmacy duty as common to every REMS. Who may dispense mifepristone, and on whose prescription, is correct, as are the pharmacy requirements (a) to (n), the 4-calendar-day rule and its prescriber-confirmation route, the transfer limits, the 180-day audits and the prescriber and Patient Agreement Form duties. The clozapine statements track the DSC: removal effective June 13, 2025; no enrollment to order; no pharmacist eligibility or ANC verification; ANC monitoring recommended to prescribers; Boxed Warning and a new Medication Guide. The one defect, Low, is quick_review[13]. Its 'not the pharmacy' wording puts Medication Guide delivery for mifepristone on the prescriber alone. That contradicts 21 CFR 208.24(e), the Mifeprex carton instruction and the section's own orientation[8]. It is a one-sentence repair. Practice mapping PASS: MA-Q-0092 (B, D), MA-Q-0106 (B, C, D), MA-Q-0402 (A) and MA-Q-0403 (D) can each be answered from the section, and neither their keys nor their explanations are contradicted. Currency note, not a defect: in Louisiana v. FDA the Fifth Circuit on May 1, 2026 ordered the in-person dispensing requirement reinstated. The Supreme Court stayed that order on May 14, 2026 (No. 25A1207) pending the appeal and any certiorari petition, so the 09/30/2025 REMS taught here remains operative on 2026-09-16. FDA's Q&A (04/08/2026) also says FDA will decide whether to change the REMS after its mifepristone safety study. Re-check REMS@FDA and that docket before any publication.
